title: Good curve presentation with a fibrewise nonempty thickening locus
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X	o S$ a separated morphism of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of an irreducible component of $S$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point], and assume $\dim X_\eta\leq1$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. There exist an open neighbourhood $U\subset S$ of $\eta$, a finite surjective universally injective morphism $V	o U$, a finite family of finite etale morphisms $T_i	o V$, and commutative diagrams over $V$ $$\coprod_iY_i\xrightarrow{
u}X_V:=X	imes_SV,\qquad Y_i\xrightarrow{j_i}\overline Y_i	o T_i	o V$$ [def-pc-fibre-product] [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], with the following properties. The map $
u$ is finite and surjective; each $j_i$ is an open immersion; $Y_i	o T_i$ is smooth and surjective; $\overline Y_i	o T_i$ is smooth and proper with geometrically connected fibres of dimension at most one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. There is an open $W\subset X_V$ such that $W_i:=
u^{-1}(W)\cap Y_i$ meets every fibre of $Y_i	o T_i$, and $
u^{-1}(W)	o W$ is a thickening, meaning a closed immersion surjective on underlying points [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. No density assertion is part of this statement. The finite family may be empty.

proof.text: Choose an affine open A containing eta. Pull back f to A. The inverse image of the generic irreducible component is an irreducible component of A, and the generic-point property follows from specialization under the open embedding. The fibre homeomorphisms identify the fibre of the restricted morphism with the original fibre, preserving its Krull dimension.
Apply the affine nonempty-thickening presentation to this restriction.

For its open B of A, take its image U in S. The image isomorphism B ≅ U transports the finite radicial cover. Pasting the two cartesian restriction squares gives an isomorphism between its curve target and the required pullback of f. Compose nu with this isomorphism and take the image of W. Transport all commutativity equations. The inverse-image open square is cartesian, so its projection is isomorphic to the original thickening projection. Closed-immersion and surjectivity properties are invariant under these isomorphisms. The point in each fibre witnessing that W is nonempty maps to a point witnessing the same property for its image.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_good_curves_nonempty_thickening
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (η : S) (hη : ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents S, IsGenericPoint η Z)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber η) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (U : S.Opens) (_ : η ∈ U) (V : Scheme.{u}) (g : V ⟶ U.toScheme),
      IsFinite g ∧ Surjective g ∧ UniversallyInjective g ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (T Y Ybar : Fin n → Scheme.{u})
        (t : ∀ i, T i ⟶ V) (j : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ Ybar i)
        (p : ∀ i, Ybar i ⟶ T i)
        (ν : (∐ Y) ⟶ pullback f (g ≫ U.ι)),
        IsFinite ν ∧ Surjective ν ∧
        (∀ i, Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν ≫ pullback.snd f (g ≫ U.ι) = j i ≫ p i ≫ t i) ∧
        (∀ i, IsFinite (t i) ∧ Etale (t i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Smooth (j i ≫ p i) ∧ Surjective (j i ≫ p i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Smooth (p i) ∧ IsProper (p i) ∧
          ∀ s : T i, GeometricallyConnected ((p i).fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
            topologicalKrullDim ((p i).fiber s) ≤ 1) ∧
        ∃ W : (pullback f (g ≫ U.ι)).Opens,
          (∀ (i : Fin n) (s : T i),
            ∃ y : (j i ≫ p i).fiber s,
              ((j i ≫ p i).fiberι s ≫ Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν) y ∈ W) ∧
          IsThickening (pullback.snd ν W.ι)
